The Addiction Care Coordinator plays a vital role in helping individuals affected by substance use disorders access compassionate, recovery-oriented care. Depending on the position, Care Coordinators work either in our hospital or outpatient NewStart Clinic, supporting patients at different stages of their recovery journey while using a harm reduction approach that meets each person where they are.

In our hospital-based role, Care Coordinators partner with patients during hospitalization to assess needs, provide education, and connect them with appropriate treatment and community resources after discharge. They collaborate with hospital care teams, patients, families, and community providers to help ensure smooth transitions into ongoing care.

In our outpatient NewStart Clinic, Care Coordinators support patients throughout their treatment experience by coordinating services, removing barriers to care, and serving as a co-facilitator in our Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) alongside a licensed therapist. The IOP provides a supportive, therapeutic group environment focused on recovery education, skill building, reducing substance use and harm, and improving functioning across health, home, purpose, and community.

No two days are the same. The ideal candidate enjoys variety, is highly organized, works independently, communicates effectively with multidisciplinary teams, and is passionate about helping individuals navigate recovery with empathy, respect, and hope.

Care Coordinators work collaboratively with Addiction Medicine physicians, therapists, nurses, and fellow Care Coordinators, while receiving regular clinical supervision and support from the NewStart leadership team

Develop and maintain project charters, workplans, timelines, milestones, and governance structures for strategic patient and family engagement initiatives
Coordinate interdisciplinary teams across hospitals, service lines, and support departments to drive project execution and accountability

For over 60 years we have maintained “A Tradition of Excellence”, serving as a trusted source for our unwavering commitment to supporting all branches of the Department of Defense and our global allies. Our collaboration extends across a diverse array of programs and platforms, including major military prime contractors such as Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, and Raytheon.

Summary

Marvin Engineering Company (MEC), a long-standing defense contractor supporting all branches of the U.S. Department of Defense and allied nations, is seeking an experienced Program Manager. For more than 60 years, MEC has partnered with major prime contractors including Lockheed Martin, Raytheon, Boeing, SAAB, and KAI on a wide range of aerospace and defense platforms. This position is based is 100% onsite.

Responsibilities

Manage all aspects of assigned contracts, including budget oversight, reporting, and adherence to product line responsibilities. Experience with Earned Value Management (EVM) is preferred.
Review contracts, purchase orders, and contract amendments.
Participate in proposal and quoting activities, including pricing and lead-time assessments.
Collaborate across functional groups—sales development, contracts, supply chain, production planning, operations, machining, quality, and engineering—to ensure on-time product delivery.
Build and maintain productive relationships with internal teams and external customers.
Prepare and present program updates and financial metrics for executive, PMO, and customer reviews.
Travel to customer sites, trade shows, or conferences as required.
Execute all duties in compliance with MEC policies and procedures.

Skills / Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline, and 5+ years of directly applicable experience; or 10+ years of relevant industry experience and/or military background in aviation, ground-based defense, or weapon systems, in lieu of a degree. Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.
U.S. Citizenship is required, along with the ability to meet federal government access requirements for controlled unclassified information.
Experience in the military, defense, or aerospace fields—particularly involving U.S. fighter, bomber, or helicopter platforms, or defense weapon systems—is highly desirable.
Demonstrated ability to develop and integrate strategies, goals, and objectives; experience coordinating cross-functional programs and resources.
Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and technical manuals.
SAP experience highly desired; proficiency in MS Office (Excel, Project, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook) required.
Professional certifications (e.g., Supply Chain Management, Project Management, Program Management, Purchasing Management, Production & Inventory Control) are preferred but not required.
Ability to multitask and work effectively in a fast-paced environment managing multiple programs.
Must be able to read, write, and speak English.
Must meet ITAR requirements as a “U.S. person” (U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, political asylee, or refugee).

This position must meet export control compliance requirements. All applicants must be “U.S. persons” within the meaning of ITAR, as defined: a U.S. Citizen, a lawful permanent resident, political asylee, or refugee.

new_jobs.description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

The Uncrewed Systems Portfolio Manager / Program Manager 3 (PM3) leads a portfolio of uncrewed systems programs and initiatives from capture through execution and closeout. This role provides integrated leadership across cost, schedule, technical performance, and customer satisfaction, while driving a disciplined program culture and ensuring required program reviews and reporting are completed. The role also serves as a key interface with customers and internal stakeholders and translates portfolio strategy into executable program roadmaps and priorities.

Key responsibilities Portfolio leadership and governance

Own and manage a portfolio of uncrewed systems programs/efforts, prioritizing scope, resources, and timelines to meet portfolio objectives.
Conduct portfolio-level program reviews (at least monthly) and ensure key functional participation; document and route deviations/waivers for approval as required.
Perform program startup reviews within 60 days of contract award/authority to proceed.

Program execution and performance management

Lead overall program execution across acquisition, execution, and closeout phases to drive successful outcomes.
Maintain accountability for program performance, including budget, schedule (including IMS contributions), and customer-facing reporting.
Establish and manage program metrics; ensure standardized monthly reporting inputs are reviewed and approved for consistency.

Customer interface and stakeholder alignment

Serve as the program’s primary interface in program relationships with the customer and coordinate across internal stakeholders to ensure aligned execution.
Prepare and deliver program reviews and briefings for customers and senior leadership.

Technical execution and digital engineering advocacy

Define program tasking and execution approach; coordinate with the customer to develop/shape the program statement of work/objectives, including digital engineering considerations as applicable.
Communicate requirements analysis approach and understand differences between traditional and model-based approaches.

Culture, compliance, and independent reviews

Foster an open, collaborative, inclusive, and disciplined program culture.
Approve and oversee the program’s independent review schedule and ensure required reviews are completed on time.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelors degree and 8 years of DOD experience
Demonstrated experience leading programs or a portfolio of programs with accountability for cost, schedule, and performance.
Experience leading cross-functional teams and conducting program reviews and executive-level briefings.
Ability to translate customer needs and program objectives into executable plans, metrics, and reporting rhythms.
Must possess an Active Secret DoD Clearance to be considered for this role.

Preferred Qualifications

Uncrewed systems domain experience (UAS/UMS/UUV/USV), mission systems integration, autonomy, C2, communications, sensors, or payload integration.
Experience implementing digital engineering practices on programs (model-based approaches, integrated digital thread).
Experience establishing portfolio-level governance, monthly review cadences, and standardized reporting.
TS/SCI Preferred

Primary Level Salary Range: $184,300.00 - $276,500.00

The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.

Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business.

The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Digital Audience Engagement
new_jobs.description:
At Franklin Templeton, we believe success is built through powerful partnerships. As a forward thinking asset manager, we build dynamic relationships with clients, understand their goals, and navigate complex markets together. We leverage cutting edge strategies and deep insights to unlock opportunities for long term wealth creation. Our talented, global teams bring expertise that is both broad and unique.

From our welcoming, inclusive, and supportive culture to our globally diverse business, we offer opportunities not only to help you reach your potential, but also to contribute to our clients’ success.

About The Department

The Franklin Innovation Research, Strategies and Technologies (FIRST) team serves as Franklin Templeton's hub for innovation, helping the firm identify, develop, and advance opportunities at the intersection of investment management and emerging technologies. The team plays a key role in shaping the firm's digital assets strategy and bringing innovative solutions to market, while fostering collaboration across business, investment, and technology functions. Through thought leadership, strategic initiatives, and experimentation with next-generation technologies, FIRST helps position Franklin Templeton at the forefront of the evolving financial services landscape.

Role Summary

The Program Manager, Digital Audience Engagement will support key initiatives that promote Franklin Templeton’s innovation and digital assets programs across B2B, B2B2C, and Direct to Wallet Audiences. Working cross-functionally with strategy, product, sales, finance, investment teams, and the broader business in a lean, start-up-like environment, the incumbent will have exposure to a variety of creative, operational, and strategic tasks within the FIRST team including:

Audience communication and digital engagement programs
Creative content, storytelling and campaign development
Project planning and timelines
Agency and 3rd party vendor relations
Owned channel management, including web/micro sites, social media...etc.
Support for executive social media and PR/media relations
New channel/platform research and analysis
Programs that leverage AI to automate, streamline and improve the quality of deliverables across the emerging solutions content team
Other operational tasks, including compliance submissions, program performance metrics and analytics

This is a hands-on role that will drive business outcomes through a fresh approach to audience engagement, supporting campaigns and creative content that leverage emerging channels and technology to highlight our innovative work across fintech, digital assets, blockchain and future-forward thought leadership. We’re looking for an entrepreneurial communicator and a strong writer that seeks room to grow in their career, and is not afraid to roll up their sleeves to tackle a wide variety of functions for the FIRST businesses and functions globally. The ideal candidate will have working knowledge of key trends across web3, blockchain, digital assets, and AI, along with demonstrated interest in next-gen audiences.

How You Will Add Value

Learn, master and manage a wide variety of digital engagement technologies and channels to enable a growing global function within Franklin Templeton
Support the development, deployment and delivery of various cross-channel communication and digital engagement campaigns across key audiences, globally
Partner with various internal shared services teams and external vendors to develop and deliver innovative content and experiences
Support all aspects of FIRST website and social media publishing, managing day-to-day changes and updates, as well as community management
Manage compliance submissions and global approvals tracking to ensure all materials are in line with relevant regulations, and record keeping is up to date
Oversee briefing, tagging and reporting process for all FIRST engagement and communications analytics across traditional and digital channels
Analyze a wide range of data to identify what is working, what is not, and how to optimize resources
Track budgets, financial reporting and manage vendor invoices
Maintain an outside-in mindset, bringing best practices from our industry and beyond to the table at Franklin Templeton to help improve our engagement across B2B and D2C audiences
Serve as an available consultant, where needed, to internal teams and external client partners on effective audience engagement trends and tactical approaches/processes

Experience

What Will Help You Be Successful in This Role

Bachelor’s degree in communications, liberal arts, marketing, journalism, or related field.
3-5 years of digital engagement or agency experience.
Experience managing digital engagement activities across multiple functions.
Experience deploying cross-channel engagement programs.
Experience with digital, mobile, social, earned, and emerging channels.
Strong writing and digital content creation skills.
Proficiency with emerging artificial intelligence (AI) tools.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
Proficiency with workplace productivity tools.
Experience in regulated industries preferred.
Start-up experience welcomed.

Soft Skills

Highly organized with strong attention to detail.
Entrepreneurial and self-directed approach.
Creative, innovative, and strategic mindset.
Ability to execute in agile environments.
Adaptable across changing priorities and projects.
Strong communication and collaboration skills.
Goal-oriented with a results-driven mindset.

This is a hybrid role that can be based out of New York City (NY), Short Hills (NJ), Baltimore (MD), Stamford (CT), or Boston (MA).

Franklin Templeton offers employees a competitive and valuable range of total rewards—monetary and non-monetary — designed to support their well-being and recognize their time, talents, and results. Along with base compensation, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, a 401(k) plan with a generous match, and recognition rewards. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package, which includes a range of competitive healthcare options, insurance, and disability benefits, employee stock investment program, learning resources, career development programs, reimbursement for certain education expenses, paid time off (vacation / holidays / sick / leave / parental & caregiving leave / bereavement / volunteering / floating holidays) and a motivational wellbeing program. We expect the annual salary for this position to range between $105,000 - $136,000, depending on location and level of relevant experience, plus discretionary bonus.

At Franklin Templeton, we believe your benefits should support your life, your goals, and your future. That’s why we offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package designed to help you thrive both personally and professionally.

Highlights Of Our Benefits Include

Paid Time Off: Three weeks of PTO in your first year
Health Coverage: Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance to support your well-being
Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with an 85% company match on pre-tax and/or Roth contributions, up to IRS limits
Equity & Investing: Employee Stock Investment Plan (ESIP) with discounted share purchase opportunities
Learning Education Assistance Program (LEAP): To support your ongoing growth and career advancement
Employee Investment Benefits: Opportunity to purchase company funds with no sales charge

Franklin Templeton is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees, and we evaluate qualified applicants without regard to ancestry, age, color, disability, genetic information, gender, gender identity, or gender expression, marital status, medical condition, military or veteran status, national origin, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, and any other basis protected by federal, state, or local law, ordinance, or regulation.

new_jobs.description:
Work Schedule

Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions

Office

Position Objective

As a Program Manager III in the Transplant Diagnostics division, you will play a pivotal role in managing projects that drive product development and on-market product improvements in alignment with business objectives. You will accomplish this by applying best practices and tools in program management with the goal of delivering high-quality research use only (RUO) and in vitro diagnostic (IVD) products to market within the agreed-upon scope, schedule, and resources. This includes ensuring design control, compliance with regulatory guidelines, and long-term product manufacturability. Through your work, you will contribute to improving the quality of life for individuals facing transplantation, while supporting Thermo Fisher Scientific’s mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Key Responsibilities

Lead cross-functional project core teams, conduct regular project meetings, capture action items, supervise assigned deliverables, develop and maintain project schedules, and provide updates and reports to senior leadership.
Work closely with R&D, Product Management, Manufacturing Sciences, and Manufacturing Operations, Quality, Regulatory, and other functional partners to develop high quality products that meet customer needs and regulatory guidelines. Collaborate with Finance and other business functions to develop project financial models and ensure positive return on investment.
Maintain clear communication lines across all teams and stakeholders, providing regular updates on project status and achievements to executives, while resolving barriers to execution and facilitating decision making to ensure timely completion.
Identify potential risks and issues, and develop effective mitigation strategies to maintain compliance, product quality, and project execution.
Identify and champion opportunities for improvement in day-to-day processes, operating mechanisms, and procedures.

Education And Experience

University degree (Bachelor’s or Master’s degree), preferably in life sciences or engineering.
Demonstrated experience leading teams without direct authority.
4 years experience in developing life-science products under design control, using a standard stage-gate process from conceptualization to launch; medical device and clinical experience highly preferred.
Experience developing RUO and IVD assays, including clinical study performance, preferred.
PMP certification is a plus.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Demonstrated excellence in project management, including timeline adherence, deliverable tracking, and proactive risk management. Capable of managing competing priorities while balancing business objectives, regulatory requirements, and customer needs.
Strong interpersonal and influencing skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across a matrixed organization and gain broad cross-functional alignment.
Exceptional written and verbal communication and presentation skills, capable of effectively articulating sophisticated concepts and ideas to broad audiences, including executives.
Self-motivated, curious, and proactive with the ability to be highly resourceful.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

Compensation And Benefits

The salary range estimated for this position based in Indiana is $83,300.00–$125,000.00.

This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:

A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy
Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan
Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount

For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

Strives to ensure member progress toward desired outcomes and contributes to overarching strategy to provide quality and cost-effective member care.

Essential Job Duties

Completes comprehensive member assessments within regulated timelines, including in-person home visits as required.
Facilitates comprehensive waiver enrollment and disenrollment processes.
Develops and implements care plans, including a waiver service plan in collaboration with members, caregivers, physicians and/or other appropriate health care professionals and member support network to address the member needs and goals.

Uses motivational interviewing and Molina clinical guideposts to educate, support and motivate change during member contacts.

Identifies critical incidents and develops prevention plans to assure member health and welfare.

Care manager RNs may be assigned complex member cases and medication regimens.
Care manager RNs may conduct medication reconciliation as needed.
25-40% estimated local travel may be required (based upon state/contractual requirements).

Required Qualifications

At least 2 years of experience in health care, including at least 1 year experience in care management, managed care, and/or experience in a medical or behavioral health setting, and at least 1 year of experience working with persons with disabilities, chronic conditions, substance abuse disorders, and long-term services and supports (LTSS), or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
Registered Nurse (RN). License must be active and unrestricted in state of practice.

Ability to operate proactively and demonstrate detail-oriented work.
Demonstrated knowledge of community resources.
Ability to work within a variety of settings and adjust style as needed - working with diverse populations and various personalities and personal situations.
Ability to work independently, with minimal supervision and demonstrate self-motivation.
Responsiveness in all forms of communication, and ability to remain calm in high-pressure situations.
Ability to develop and maintain professional relationships.
Time-management and prioritization skills, and ability to focus on multiple projects simultaneously and adapt to change.
Problem-solving skills.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Microsoft Office suite/applicable software program(s) proficiency.

Certified Case Manager (CCM).
Experience working with populations that receive waiver services.
